# Blueprint nodes and components {#ch17}



## Playing and stopping recipes {#ref_nodes_play}

These nodes are in the **Feel** category of the Blueprint context menu.

[shot: S17-01 | The Blueprint context menu searched for Feel]

### Play Feel {#node_play_feel}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Plays a recipe.

The returned handle is invalid when the recipe could not start: no recipe was given, a **Cooldown** or **Max Concurrent** limit of the recipe is reached on this target, `feel.Enabled` is 0, the game runs as a dedicated server, or the target is an actor or component that no longer exists (this last case also logs a warning).

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::PlayFeel`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | In | Feel Recipe |  | The recipe to play. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What the recipe plays on. Camera and screen effects go to the target's local player. |
| **Intensity** | In | Float | 1 | Multiplier for every track of this play. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Handle |  | Handle to stop or query this play. Invalid if the recipe could not start (cooldown, max concurrent, or feel.Enabled 0). |

### Play Feel with Context {#node_play_feel_with_context}

[edition: Pro]

Plays a recipe like Play Feel, with extra information for this play. Use it when the recipe declares parameters, has tracks that apply to a second actor, or uses context tags.

- Parameters: values for the recipe's parameters; tracks with parameter mappings scale their intensity by them.
- Instigator: a second actor; tracks set to Applies To = Instigator play their actor effects on it.
- Direction, Location, Normal, Context Tags: passed to steps and Blueprint events, and used by Feel Maps.

With an empty context this behaves exactly like Play Feel.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::PlayFeelWithContext`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | In | Feel Recipe |  | The recipe to play. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What the recipe plays on. |
| **Context** | In | Feel Play Context |  | Parameter values, second actor and details for this play. Every field is optional. Can be left unconnected. |
| **Intensity** | In | Float | 1 | Multiplier for every track of this play. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Handle |  | Handle to stop or query this play. Invalid if the recipe could not start. |

### Play Feel and Wait {#node_play_feel_and_wait}

[edition: Pro]

Plays a recipe and waits for it to end. On Finished fires when the recipe plays to its end. On Cancelled fires when it is stopped early, its target is destroyed, or it could not start (cooldown, max concurrent, feel.Enabled 0).

- **Node:** Latent node with an output execution pin for each outcome.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelPlayAndWaitAction::PlayFeelAndWait`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | In | Feel Recipe |  | The recipe to play. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What the recipe plays on. |
| **Context** | In | Feel Play Context |  | Optional parameter values, second actor and details for this play. Can be left unconnected. |
| **Intensity** | In | Float | 1 | Multiplier for every track of this play. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Play and Wait Action |  |  |

## Targets {#ref_nodes_targets}

A Feel Target left at its default (type None) sends camera and screen effects to the first local player. A target that belongs to a player on another machine gets no camera, screen or controller effects on this machine; that player's own machine shows them.

### Make Feel Target from Actor {#node_target_from_actor}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Target an actor. Actor effects such as Scale Punch use its root component; when the root takes part in collision (a character's capsule), they use its visible child components instead, so collision and movement stay unchanged.

Use this node for characters: scale, wobble and other actor motion then go to the character's mesh and never move its capsule.

- **Node:** Pure node, no execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::MakeFeelTargetFromActor`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Actor** | In | Actor |  | The actor to play on. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Target |  | The target. |

### Feel Target structure {#ref_feel_target}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

What a recipe plays on.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Type** | None | Kind of target. |
| **Actor** | None | Target actor when Type is Actor. Shown only when **Type** is **Actor**. |
| **Component** | None | Target component when Type is Scene Component. Shown only when **Type** is **Scene Component**. |
| **Location** | (0, 0, 0) | World location when Type is World Location. Shown only when **Type** is **World Location**. |
| **Local Player Index** | 0 | Index of the local player when Type is Local Player Camera. At least 0. Shown only when **Type** is **Local Player Camera**. |
| **Widget** | None | Target widget when Type is Widget. Shown only when **Type** is **Widget**. |

Values of **Type**:

- **None**: No target: camera and screen effects go to the first local player.
- **Actor**: An actor; actor effects use its root component, or its visible child components when the root takes part in collision (such as a character's capsule).
- **Scene Component**: A specific scene component.
- **World Location**: A point in the world.
- **Local Player Camera**: The camera of a local player.
- **Widget**: A UMG widget. Widget steps apply to it; camera and screen effects go to its owning player.

## Play context {#ref_nodes_context}

In Blueprint, build the structure with **Make FeelPlayContext** and connect it to the **Context** pin of Play Feel with Context, Send Feel Event, Play Feel and Wait or the networked nodes. Every field is optional.

### Feel Play Context structure {#ref_play_context}

[edition: Pro]

Extra information passed with a play. Everything is optional; an empty context plays the recipe exactly like Play Feel. It carries values for the recipe's parameters, an optional second actor that tracks can apply to, and details about what triggered the play that steps and Blueprint events can read.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Parameters** | empty | Values for the recipe's parameters, by parameter name. Parameters not listed use their default value. |
| **Instigator** | None | A second actor involved in this play, besides the target: whatever caused or started it. Tracks whose Applies To is Instigator play their actor effects on this actor instead of the target. Leave empty when only the target matters. |
| **Direction** | (0, 0, 0) | A world-space direction associated with the play, if any. Zero means none. |
| **Location** | (0, 0, 0) | A world-space location associated with the play, when it differs from the target's location. Zero means none. |
| **Normal** | (0, 0, 0) | A world-space surface normal associated with the play, if any. Zero means none. |
| **Context Tags** | empty | Gameplay tags describing the circumstances of the play. Feel Maps use them to choose between recipe variants. |

## Parameters and accumulators {#ref_nodes_parameters}

**Set Feel Parameter** changes a value of one play. The accumulator nodes change named values that any play can read through a recipe parameter's **Accumulator** field; accumulators are defined in the project settings ([see: set_playback]). The name pins of the accumulator nodes are dropdowns that list the accumulators of the project.

### Set Feel Parameter {#node_set_feel_parameter}

[edition: Pro]

Changes a parameter of a recipe that is playing. Tracks mapped to the parameter follow the new value from the next frame. Useful for sustained recipes whose strength follows a changing value.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::SetFeelParameter`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Handle** | In | Feel Handle |  | Handle returned when the recipe started. |
| **Parameter Name** | In | Name |  | Name of a parameter the recipe declares. The dropdown lists the parameters of the recipe played by the node the Handle comes from, or every recipe parameter in the project. |
| **Value** | In | Float |  | New value. Clamped to the parameter's range. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Boolean |  | False when the recipe is no longer playing. |

### Add to Feel Accumulator {#node_add_to_accumulator}

[edition: Pro]

Adds to an accumulator (Project Settings > Plugins > FeelKit > Accumulators). The value is clamped to the accumulator's max and decays over time. Recipe parameters that read the accumulator follow it.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel > Accumulators.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::AddToFeelAccumulator`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Accumulator Name** | In | Name |  | Name of the accumulator. |
| **Amount** | In | Float |  | Amount to add. Negative amounts subtract. |
| **Actor** | In | Actor | None | Actor the value belongs to. Leave empty for the global value. |

### Set Feel Accumulator {#node_set_accumulator}

[edition: Pro]

Sets an accumulator to a value, clamped to its max.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel > Accumulators.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::SetFeelAccumulator`.

| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |

## Events and Feel Maps {#ref_nodes_events}

### Send Feel Event {#node_send_feel_event}

[edition: Pro]

Sends a named event and plays the recipe a Feel Map assigns to it. The map row is chosen by the event tag and the context tags: the most specific match wins. Maps on a Feel Trigger component of the target actor are checked before the project's maps (Project Settings > Plugins > FeelKit > Feel Maps). Use it to keep gameplay code free of recipe choices: gameplay sends what happened, the maps decide how it feels.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::SendFeelEvent`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Event** | In | Gameplay Tag |  | Event tag to look up. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What the recipe plays on. |
| **Context** | In | Feel Play Context |  | Optional parameter values, second actor, details and context tags. Can be left unconnected. |
| **Intensity** | In | Float | 1 | Multiplier for every track of this play, multiplied by the row's intensity scale. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Handle |  | Handle of the play. Invalid when no row matches or the recipe could not start. |

### Feel Map asset {#ref_feel_map}

[edition: Pro]

Decides which recipe plays for a named event. Gameplay sends an event tag with a play context; the map picks the row that matches most specifically, so variants for different circumstances need no branching in Blueprint. Matching: the row's event must match the sent event (same tag or a parent), and the context must contain all of the row's required tags. Among matches, a more specific event wins, then more required tags, then higher priority, then the earlier row.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Entries** | empty | Rows of this map. |

Each entry of **Entries**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Event** | None | Event this row answers. Also answers child events: a row for A.B answers A.B.C when no row is more specific. |
| **Required Tags** | empty | Tags the play context must all contain for this row to apply. Empty applies in every circumstance. |
| **Recipe** | None | Recipe to play. |
| **Intensity Scale** | 1 | Multiplies the intensity of the event when this row plays. At least 0. |
| **Priority** | 0 | Breaks ties between rows that match equally specifically. Higher wins. |

## Comfort {#ref_nodes_comfort}

Comfort settings belong to a local player. **Get Feel Comfort** returns the player's Feel Comfort Subsystem, and the other comfort nodes are called on it. The settings are loaded when the local player is created, before any recipe plays, and saved automatically after each change while **Auto Save Comfort** is on ([see: set_comfort_storage]).

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Values of **Group**:

- **Screen Distortion**: Vignette, chromatic aberration and other distortion.
- **Haptics**: Controller vibration.

## Feel Switch {#ref_nodes_switch}

**Set Feel Enabled**, **Toggle Feel** and **Is Feel Enabled** work with or without a Feel Switch actor in the level. They change and read the same value as the console variable `feel.Enabled` ([see: con_feel_enabled]).

### Set Feel Enabled {#node_set_feel_enabled}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Turns all FeelKit feedback off or on, for comparing a game with and without it. Off stops every playing recipe at once (slowed time returns to normal) and nothing new plays until it is turned on again. Only FeelKit is affected: the game's own camera shakes, sounds and effects keep working. Same switch as the console variable feel.Enabled; applies to the whole game on this machine and is not saved.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Category:** Feel > Switch.
- **C++:** `UFeelBlueprintLibrary::SetFeelEnabled`.

[edition: Lite and Pro]

### Feel Switch actor {#ref_feel_switch}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Lets players turn FeelKit off and on while playing, to see and feel the difference. Place one in a level: it shows a start card that explains the switch, keeps a small ON/OFF badge in a corner of the screen, and switches when a player presses one of the Switch Keys (keyboard or controller). No input assets or Blueprint changes are needed: the keys are read from each local player's own key presses, next to whatever input setup the game uses. Off stops only FeelKit (see Set Feel Enabled); the game's own effects keep working. The Comfort Menu Keys open the player's comfort menu, so players can also try the comfort settings while playing.

Place one Feel Switch in a level. A second one in the same level logs a warning and does nothing. The switch applies to the whole game on this machine, so every Play In Editor window switches together, and the choice is not saved.

|---|---|---|
| >> Feel Switch |  |  |
| **Switch Keys** | Tab, Gamepad Special Left | Keys and controller buttons that turn the feel off and on. The first keyboard key and the first controller button are named on the start card and the badge. |

| >> Feel Switch > Display |  |  |

| **Show Start Card** | On | Show a card when the level starts that explains how to switch. It fades after Start Card Seconds or on any key or button. Editable only when **Show Built in Display** is on. |

| **Start Card Text** | "Everything you see, hear and feel on top of the game comes from FeelKit." | One or two lines under the heading, for example what this level shows. Leave empty for none. Editable only when **Show Built in Display** is on and **Show Start Card** is on. |
| **Start Card Seconds** | 8 s | Seconds (real time) the start card stays before it fades, unless a key or button is pressed first. At least 1. Editable only when **Show Built in Display** is on and **Show Start Card** is on. |
| **Controls** | empty | The level's controls, shown in a small panel under the badge for as long as the level runs. Leave empty for no panel. Editable only when **Show Built in Display** is on. |
| >> Feel Switch > Comfort Menu |  |  |

| **Comfort Menu Class** | None | Menu to open. Empty uses Comfort Menu Class from Project Settings > Plugins > FeelKit. |
| **Pause in Comfort Menu** | On | Pause the game while the comfort menu is open. The menu's previews still play. |

Event **On Feel Switched** with **Feel Enabled** (Boolean): Called whenever FeelKit is turned off or on, from a Switch Key, a Blueprint node or the console variable feel.Enabled.

Add these to an animation's **Notifies** track (right-click the track, **Add Notify** or **Add Notify State**). They play when the animation reaches them in the game, and also in the animation editor's preview, so actor effects can be tuned while scrubbing the animation.

## Feel Trigger component {#ref_nodes_trigger}

### Feel Trigger {#ref_feel_trigger}

[edition: Pro]

Plays recipes or sends Feel Events when common events happen to its owner, with no Blueprint wiring. Also holds Feel Maps that Send Feel Event checks first when this actor is the target.

The component ticks only when one of its entries uses Jumped, Air Jumped or Launched, because those have no engine event to bind to. The other events are bound when play begins.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Triggers** | empty | What to play for each event. Several entries may use the same event. |
| **Feel Maps** | empty | Feel Maps checked before the project's maps when a Feel Event targets this actor. |

Each entry of **Triggers**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Event** | Take Any Damage | Actor event that fires this entry. |
| **Recipe** | None | Recipe to play. When empty, Feel Event is sent instead. |
| **Feel Event** | None | Event sent through the Feel Maps when no recipe is set, so maps choose the recipe. Editable only when **Recipe** is empty. |
| **Value Parameter** | None | Recipe parameter that receives the event value (damage amount, landing speed or hit impulse). Map that parameter on tracks to scale them by it. Leave empty to ignore the value. |
| **Intensity** | 1 | Intensity of the play. At least 0. |
| **Target Skeletal Mesh** | On | Play on the owner's first skeletal mesh component instead of the owner actor, so actor effects such as scale apply to the visible mesh of characters rather than their collision capsule. |
| **Other Actor as Instigator** | On | Pass the other actor of the event (damage causer, hit or overlapping actor) as the play's instigator. When the entry plays on the other actor, the owner becomes the instigator instead. |
| **Play On** | Owner | Where the recipe plays: on the owner, or on the other actor of the event. |
| **Only for Players** | Off | Fire only when the other actor of the event is a pawn controlled by a player (or that player's controller), so enemies, props or projectiles do not set it off. |
| **Context Tags** | empty | Context tags added to every play of this entry. |

#### Fire Event

[edition: Pro]

Fires every entry for an event, as if it happened. Useful for events the component does not bind itself.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Target:** Feel Trigger component.
- **Category:** Feel.
- **C++:** `UFeelTriggerComponent::FireEvent`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Event** | In | Feel Trigger Event |  | Which entries to fire: those set to this event. |
| **Event Value** | In | Float |  | The event's value, passed to each entry's Value Parameter (for example a fall speed or damage). |
| **Other Actor** | In | Actor |  | The other actor of the event, used by Other Actor As Instigator and Play On Other Actor. Can be empty. |

Values of **Event**, with the event value each one passes:

- **Take Any Damage**: The owner receives damage (any damage type). Event value: the damage amount.
- **Landed**: The owner, a Character, lands after falling. Event value: the downward speed at landing, in cm/s.
- **Component Hit**: The owner's root component reports a blocking hit. Event value: the length of the normal impulse.
- **Begin Overlap**: Another actor starts overlapping the owner. Event value: 0.
- **End Overlap**: Another actor stops overlapping the owner. Event value: 0.
- **Jumped**: The owner, a Character, jumps from the ground (including a late jump just after walking off a ledge). Event value: the jump number, 1.
- **Air Jumped**: The owner, a Character, jumps again while already in the air (double or triple jump). Event value: the jump number, 2 or more.
- **Launched**: The owner, a Character, is launched: thrown by gameplay rather than by its own movement, such as a wall jump, a jump pad or a knockback (Launch Character). Event value: the launch speed in cm/s. The play's Direction is the launch direction.

## Feel Input component {#ref_nodes_input}

### Feel Input {#ref_feel_input}

[edition: Pro]

Plays FeelKit recipes from Enhanced Input actions without Blueprint wiring. Add it to a pawn or a player controller and list the actions to respond to. Plays target the owning actor. Bindings attach to the owner's input component once it exists and are attached again when the pawn is possessed by a new controller.

The input actions must be in an input mapping context that the player has added.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Bindings** | empty | Actions this component responds to. |

Each entry of **Bindings**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Action** | None | The input action to listen to. It must be in an input mapping context the player has added. |
| **Play On** | Started | When to play: Started (the input begins), Triggered (each time the action's triggers fire; every frame while held for a plain press), Completed or Canceled. |
| **Recipe** | None | Recipe to play. When empty, Event is sent instead. |
| **Event** | None | Feel Event to send when no recipe is set. |
| **Intensity** | 1 | Intensity of the play. At least 0. |
| **Scale Intensity by Value** | Off | Multiplies the intensity by the action value's magnitude, clamped to 0 to 1 (for example how far a trigger is pressed). |
| **Value Parameter** | None | Recipe parameter that receives the action value's magnitude. Empty sends none. |
| **End when Input Ends** | Off | Ends the play when the input ends (Completed or Canceled), for feedback that lasts while the input is held, such as a charge-up. A sustained recipe is released and plays its ending; other recipes stop with a blend out. |
| **Once Per Press** | Off | Plays at most once until the input ends, even when Play On fires repeatedly (such as Triggered while held). |

Responds to one binding as if its action fired. Used by the input bindings; callable to simulate input.

## Feel Replication component {#ref_nodes_replication}

### Feel Replication {#ref_feel_replication}

[edition: Pro]

Plays recipes and sends Feel Events on several machines in a networked game. Add it to a replicated actor, such as a character or a weapon. Called on the server, the request goes to the machines the mode selects. Called on the client that owns the actor, the client plays at once (no wait for the server) and the server forwards the play to everyone else. Called on any other client, the play stays local. Only the request is sent; each machine evaluates the recipe with its own comfort settings. Plays are cosmetic and unreliable: under heavy packet loss a remote machine may miss one.

Add it to a replicated actor, such as a character or a weapon. The component is replicated by default.

#### Play Feel Networked

[edition: Pro]

Plays a recipe on the machines chosen by Mode.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Target:** Feel Replication component.
- **Category:** Feel > Network.
- **C++:** `UFeelReplicationComponent::PlayFeelNetworked`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | In | Feel Recipe |  | Recipe to play. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What it plays on. Actors and components must exist on every machine (replicated or placed in the level). |
| **Intensity** | In | Float |  | Strength of the play, as in Play Feel. |
| **Context** | In | Feel Play Context |  | Parameters, instigator, direction, location, normal and tags of the play. Can be left unconnected. |
| **Mode** | In | Feel Net Mode | Everyone | Which machines play it. |
| **Relevancy Distance** | In | Float | 0 | Machines whose local players are all farther than this from the target (measured from each player's character or camera, whichever is closer) skip the play. A player's own character is always in range. 0 means no limit. Shown under the node's advanced arrow. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Handle |  | Handle of the play on this machine, invalid when this machine does not play it. |

#### Send Feel Event Networked

[edition: Pro]

Sends a Feel Event on the machines chosen by Mode. Each machine picks the recipe from its Feel Maps.

- **Node:** Callable node with execution pins.
- **Target:** Feel Replication component.
- **Category:** Feel > Network.
- **C++:** `UFeelReplicationComponent::SendFeelEventNetworked`.

{widths: 20,9,17,11,43}
| Pin | In or out | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Event** | In | Gameplay Tag |  | Event tag. |
| **Target** | In | Feel Target |  | What it plays on. Actors and components must exist on every machine. |
| **Intensity** | In | Float |  | Strength of the play. |
| **Context** | In | Feel Play Context |  | Parameters, instigator, direction, location, normal and tags of the play. Can be left unconnected. |
| **Mode** | In | Feel Net Mode | Everyone | Which machines play it. |
| **Relevancy Distance** | In | Float | 0 | Machines whose local players are all farther than this from the target (measured from each player's character or camera, whichever is closer) skip the play. A player's own character is always in range. 0 means no limit. Shown under the node's advanced arrow. |
| **Return Value** | Out | Feel Handle |  | Handle of the play on this machine, invalid when this machine does not play it or no map entry matched. |

Values of **Mode**:

- **Everyone**: Every machine plays it.
- **Owner Only**: Only the machine that owns this component's actor plays it, for feedback meant for one player. The actor must be owned by a player (its pawn, controller or something they own).
- **Skip Owner**: Every machine except the owner's plays it, for feedback the owner already played locally. In a single-player game nothing plays.

These classes are in the GAS add-on, the separate plugin FeelKit GAS with the module FeelGAS. It is not active until you copy it into your project. To use one in Blueprint, create a Blueprint class with the class below as its parent and set its **Gameplay Cue Tag** as for any other gameplay cue notify.

### Feel Gameplay Cue Notify {#ref_cue_notify}

[edition: Pro]

Gameplay Cue notify that plays a FeelKit recipe or sends a Feel Event when the cue is executed or added. For one-shot feedback such as hits and pickups. For feedback that lasts while a gameplay effect is active, use Feel Gameplay Cue Notify (Actor). Set the Gameplay Cue Tag as for any static cue notify.

[edition: Pro]

Gameplay Cue notify actor that plays a FeelKit recipe while its gameplay cue is active: it starts when the cue is added and ends when the cue is removed (see Stop On Remove). Use a recipe with a sustain region for feedback that loops for as long as the effect lasts.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | None | Recipe to play. When empty, Event is sent instead. |

## C++ access {#ref_cpp}

FeelKit's runtime module is FeelCore. Add it to the dependencies of your game module in its `.Build.cs` file; add FeelEnhancedInput to use the Feel Input component from C++, and FeelGAS for the GAS add-on.

```
PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[] { "Core", "CoreUObject", "Engine", "FeelCore" });
```

Plays go through the world's Feel Subsystem:

```
#include "FeelSubsystem.h"

if (UFeelSubsystem* Feel = UFeelSubsystem::Get(this))
{
    HitHandle = Feel->PlayFeel(HitRecipe, FFeelTarget::FromActor(this));
}
```

Here `HitRecipe` is a `UFeelRecipe` property of the class and `HitHandle` an `FFeelHandle` member. `FFeelTarget` has the static functions `FromActor`, `FromComponent`, `AtLocation`, `FromLocalPlayerCamera` and `FromWidget`, which match the Make Feel Target nodes. The nodes in the **Feel** categories are static functions of `UFeelBlueprintLibrary` and can be called from C++ as well. The table lists the functions of `UFeelSubsystem` for C++ code.

{widths: 42,44,14}
| Declaration | What it does | Edition |
|---|---|---|
| `static UFeelSubsystem* Get(const UObject* WorldContextObject)` | Subsystem of the world of WorldContextObject, or null. | Lite and Pro |
| `FFeelHandle PlayFeel(UFeelRecipe* Recipe, const FFeelTarget& Target, float Intensity = 1.0f, const FFeelPlayContext& Context = FFeelPlayContext())` | Starts a recipe. Returns an invalid handle when it cannot start (null recipe, cooldown, max concurrent, feel.Enabled 0, dedicated server). Context carries optional parameter values, a second actor and details for this play. | Lite and Pro |
| `FFeelHandle SendFeelEvent(const FGameplayTag& Event, const FFeelTarget& Target, float Intensity = 1.0f, const FFeelPlayContext& Context = FFeelPlayContext())` | Plays the recipe a Feel Map assigns to an event, chosen by the event tag and the context tags. Maps on a Feel Trigger component of the target actor are checked before the project's maps. Returns an invalid handle when no row matches. | Pro |
| `void StopFeel(FFeelHandle Handle, bool bBlendOut)` | Stops one instance, optionally fading it out over the project's blend-out time. | Lite and Pro |
| `void ReleaseFeel(FFeelHandle Handle)` | Ends the sustain loop of a sustained recipe so it plays to the end. Recipes without sustain are unaffected. | Pro |
| `void StopAllFeel(const AActor* Target = nullptr)` | Stops every instance, or only those playing on Target when it is set. | Lite and Pro |
| `bool SetFeelParameter(FFeelHandle Handle, FName ParameterName, float Value)` | Changes a parameter of a playing recipe. Takes effect on the next frame. Returns false when the play has ended. | Pro |
| `bool IsPlaying(FFeelHandle Handle) const` | True while the instance of Handle is playing (including while blending out). | Lite and Pro |
| `int32 GetNumActiveInstances() const` | Number of instances that have not finished. | Lite and Pro |
| `void AddToAccumulator(FName AccumulatorName, float Amount, const AActor* Actor = nullptr)` | Adds to an accumulator for an actor, or the global value when Actor is null. Clamped to the accumulator's max. | Pro |
| `void SetAccumulator(FName AccumulatorName, float Value, const AActor* Actor = nullptr)` | Sets an accumulator for an actor, or the global value when Actor is null. | Pro |
| `float GetAccumulator(FName AccumulatorName, const AActor* Actor = nullptr) const` | Current accumulator value for an actor, or the global value when Actor is null. 0 when never set. | Pro |
| `FOnFeelStarted OnFeelStarted` (FFeelHandle Handle, UFeelRecipe* Recipe) | Broadcast when a recipe starts playing. | Pro |
| `FOnFeelFinished OnFeelFinished` (FFeelHandle Handle, UFeelRecipe* Recipe, bool bInterrupted) | Broadcast when a recipe stops: bInterrupted is false when it played to the end. | Pro |
